name.description: Name of the API, used in documentation and generated type prefixes.

version.description: API version segment, for example v1.

base_path.description: Prefix every route sits under, for example /api/v1.

permissions.description: Whether generated handlers check a permission derived from the resource and operation. Defaults to derived.

search_method.description: How the Search operation is exposed. Defaults to both: QUERY with a POST alias.

revision_header.description: Header carrying the API revision, in both directions. Defaults to API-Revision.

enabled.description: Whether this project authenticates its callers. The server-go generator writes the wiring only when it is set.

base_path.description: Prefix the authentication endpoints sit under. Defaults to /auth.

tenant.description: How a request names the tenant it is for.

session.description: How long the credentials somebody holds stay valid.

password.description: What a new password must satisfy.

limits.description: Rate limits, counted in the database so replicas cannot disagree.

allow_registration.description: Mount the registration endpoint, where a stranger creates an account. Off means the route does not exist.

allow_tenant_creation.description: Mount the tenant-creation endpoint. Who may create one, and what else a new one needs, stay in Go.

require_verified_email.description: Refuse a sign-in until the address has been verified.

trusted_proxies.description: CIDR ranges whose X-Forwarded-For may be believed, for example 10.0.0.0/8. Empty trusts none of them.

log_retention.description: How long an entry in rig_auth_log is kept, for example 90d. Zero, the default, keeps everything. It cannot be shorter than the longest rate-limit window, because this table is what the limits count.

oauth.description: Provider sign-in. No providers means the provider routes are not mounted.

expose.description: Foundation tables to generate a model, repository, and API for anyway.

own.description: Generate for every foundation table, for a project that has forked the schema and no longer imports rig/auth.

max.description: How many are allowed in one window.

login_by_email.description: Failed sign-ins per address before the account is locked out. Defaults to 5 per 15m.

login_by_ip.description: Failed sign-ins per source address. Looser than the per-address limit so an office behind one NAT does not trip it. Defaults to 50 per 15m.

password_reset.description: Password-reset requests per address. Defaults to 5 per 1h.

verification_resend.description: Verification mails per address. Defaults to 5 per 1h.

refresh.description: Token rotations per session. A client refreshing this often is looping, not working. Defaults to 60 per 1m.

api_key_failures.description: Failed API-key authentications per key. Defaults to 20 per 1m.

base_url.description: This application's own origin, for example https://app.example.com. The callback URL is built from it and a provider compares that exactly.

base_url_env.description: Environment variable that overrides base_url, for an origin that differs per deployment. Not defaulted: one of base_url and base_url_env has to be set.

origin_from_host.description: Derive the callback origin from each request's Host, for an application serving a tenant per subdomain. Every origin must be registered with the provider.

signing_key_env.description: Environment variable holding the key that signs the state parameter, at least 32 bytes. Defaults to OAUTH_SIGNING_KEY. Unset generates one per process, which breaks across replicas.

state_ttl.description: How long a sign-in round trip may take. Generous for a redirect, short enough that a stolen state is useless. Defaults to 10m.

allow_provisioning.description: Create an account the first time somebody signs in with a provider. Off means a provider sign-in only works for an address that already has one.

allowed_return_to.description: Origins or paths a finished sign-in may return to. Anything else is refused, which is what stops an open redirect.

insecure.description: Allow the state cookie over plain HTTP, for local development only. Never set this in a deployment.

providers.description: Identity providers to offer. Empty mounts no provider routes.

min_length.description: Minimum password length in characters. Defaults to 12.

max_length.description: Maximum password length in characters. This bounds hashing work, not strength. Defaults to 1024.

breach_check.description: Reject passwords that appear in Have I Been Pwned. Only a hash prefix is sent, and the check fails open.

name.description: Which provider. It is also the route segment: google is reached at <base_path>/oauth/google/start.

client_id_env.description: Environment variable holding the client id. Defaults to <PROVIDER>_CLIENT_ID.

client_secret_env.description: Environment variable holding the client secret. Defaults to <PROVIDER>_CLIENT_SECRET.

tenant_env.description: Microsoft only: environment variable naming its directory. common accepts any account, a directory id restricts sign-in to one organization. Defaults to MICROSOFT_TENANT.

required.description: Fail startup when the credentials are absent. The default skips the provider instead, so one configuration works with or without them.

access_ttl.description: Lifetime of the access token, which travels on every request. Shorter is safer and refreshes more often. Defaults to 10m.

refresh_ttl.description: How long an ordinary session lasts. Defaults to 12h.

remember_ttl.description: How long a session lasts when somebody asked to stay signed in. Defaults to 30d.

rotation_leeway.description: How long a refresh token stays usable after it was exchanged, so a dropped response is a retry rather than a logout. Longer forgives more retries and widens the replay window. Defaults to 30s.

identity_ttl.description: Lifetime of the tenant-less credential held between signing in and picking a tenant. Defaults to 30m.

from.description: Sources to try in order; the first that names a tenant wins. Defaults to [header].

header.description: Header the header source reads. Defaults to X-Tenant-Id.

query.description: Query parameter the query source reads. Defaults to tenant.

default_slug_env.description: Environment variable holding a tenant slug to fall back to when the host names none.

enabled.description: Whether reads are held in memory between requests — session and API key verification, and the Get of any table setting cache: true — behind a Postgres NOTIFY channel that invalidates them. Off by default.

ttl.description: How long a cached answer may be reused when no invalidation arrives. It is the backstop, not the guarantee: a revocation is published on the transaction that made it. Defaults to 30s.

channel.description: The Postgres NOTIFY channel invalidations travel on. Two deployments sharing one database and not wanting to share invalidations is the reason it is configurable. Defaults to rig_cache.

max_entries.description: How many entries one cache may hold before it is dropped whole. Defaults to 50000.

image.description: Container image for the throwaway database.

port.description: Host port the throwaway database listens on.

password.description: Database password. This is a local throwaway database; do not put a real secret here.

schema.description: Postgres schema to read. Defaults to public.

settings.description: Extra Postgres server parameters for the throwaway container, passed as -c name=value flags.

electric.description: An ElectricSQL sync-service container managed beside the throwaway database.

url.description: Connection URL of an existing database. Set this to skip the throwaway container entirely.

enabled.description: Start an ElectricSQL container beside the throwaway database.

image.description: Container image for the sync service.

port.description: Host port the sync service listens on.

Duration.description: A length of time: 250ms, 30s, 15m, 12h, 30d. Go's duration syntax, with d for days.

enabled.description: Whether this project accepts uploads. The server-go generator writes the wiring only when it is set.

expose.description: Project rig_file as a read-only resource, so its url column can be read and synced. There is no generated write path either way.

backend.description: Where the bytes are kept. memory is for tests and go run and is not durable. Defaults to memory.

s3.description: Bucket settings, read only when backend is s3.

max_bytes.description: Largest single upload, in bytes. A hard per-file cap, not a storage quota. Defaults to 26214400 (25 MiB).

inline_types.description: Sniffed content types served inline rather than as an attachment. Kept short: a file served inline from the API origin runs there. Defaults to common image types.

abandoned_after.description: How long a file row with no bytes behind it is left alone before the sweeper reaps it. Defaults to 24h.

restore_window.description: How long a deleted file stays restorable, and how long its bytes outlive the delete. A bucket lifecycle rule has to outlive it. Defaults to 720h (30 days).

cookie_downloads.description: Accept the session cookie on file download routes, so a stored URL works in an img or a download link. GET only, deliberately: widening it past GET reintroduces the CSRF problem bearer tokens avoid.

bucket.description: Bucket name. One of bucket and bucket_env has to be set.

bucket_env.description: Environment variable holding the bucket name, for a bucket that differs per deployment.

endpoint.description: Endpoint URL, for an S3-compatible service that is not AWS.

access_key_env.description: Environment variable holding the access key id. Defaults to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.

secret_key_env.description: Environment variable holding the secret access key. Defaults to AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

name.description: Registered generator name, for example persist-go.

out_dir.description: Output directory, relative to the project root.

options.description: Generator-specific options. Each generator publishes its own schema for this block.

table_dir.description: Directory for a table's configuration and service code. Templates: {table} {Table} {tables}.

config_file.description: Path to a table's configuration file. May reference {table_dir}.

table.description: Name of the migration bookkeeping table.

foundation.description: Who keeps rig's own migrations. vendored copies them into this project's migrations directory; embedded leaves each module to apply its own. Defaults to vendored, and cannot be changed once the database exists.

enabled.description: Whether this project serves rig's monitoring page. It requires tracing.enabled, because the spans are what the page reads.

addr.description: Where the monitoring page listens, as host:port, for example 127.0.0.1:9090. Required when monitoring.enabled is set; there is no default. $RIG_MONITOR_ADDR overrides it at run time.

base_path.description: Where the page is mounted on its own listener. Defaults to /_rig/monitor.

max_traces.description: How many requests the page lists, newest first. Defaults to 200.

max_logs.description: How many log lines the page reads, newest first. Defaults to 500.

password_env.description: Variable the page reads its password from. Defaults to RIG_MONITOR_PASSWORD. Empty at run time means the page does not listen at all.

password.description: The page's password, written here rather than read from the environment. It warns: rig.yaml is checked in.

allow.description: Addresses that may reach the page, as CIDR ranges or single addresses, for example 10.0.0.0/8 or 127.0.0.1. Empty allows any. It narrows the password check rather than replacing it, and is matched against the connection's own address, never a forwarded header.

json_case.description: Shape of generated JSON keys. Defaults to camel.

initialisms.description: Extra acronyms that stay uppercase in Go identifiers, for example SCB.

plurals.description: Plural overrides keyed by table name, for the words English inflection gets wrong.

enabled.description: Whether this project has an inbox. The server-go generator writes the wiring only when it is set.

expose.description: Project the inbox as a generated resource as well, for the filter grammar and a typed client. The hand-written routes exist either way.

default_digest.description: What an account gets on a channel it has no setting for. Defaults to Immediate.

claim_ttl.description: How long a dispatcher's claim on a delivery is honoured before another may take it. Set it longer than your slowest channel's timeout. Defaults to 5m, and under 1m is refused.

send_timeout.description: How long one call into a channel may take before it is treated as failed. Has to be shorter than claim_ttl. Defaults to 30s, and under 1s is refused.

max_attempts.description: How many times a delivery is tried before it is marked failed. Defaults to 14, which with the default base and cap spans about eight hours.

backoff_base.description: Delay before the first retry. Each attempt doubles it, up to backoff_cap. Defaults to 1m.

backoff_cap.description: The longest one retry delay may be, once the doubling reaches it. Has to be at least backoff_base. Defaults to 1h.

retention.description: How long a read and deleted inbox line is kept before it is pruned. Has to outlive the longest digest window. Defaults to 2160h (90 days).

enabled.description: Whether this project tracks presence. The server-go generator writes the wiring only when it is set.

expose.description: Project presence as a generated read-only resource as well, for the filter grammar and a typed client. The hand-written routes and the live shape exist either way.

ttl.description: How long a session stays present after its last heartbeat. Defaults to 1m; under 15s is refused, and it has to be at least three times heartbeat.

heartbeat.description: How often a browser confirms it is still there. Defaults to 20s. Every beat is one row change fanned out to every subscriber, so this is the write rate rather than a latency knob.

sweep.description: How often the in-process sweeper ticks when it is running. Defaults to 1m. Whether it runs at all is a line in main.go, not a value here.

grace.description: How long past the TTL a row survives before the sweeper removes it. Defaults to 5m. It is what keeps a row from being deleted while a subscriber is still deciding about it.

module.description: Go module path of the application, used to build generated import paths.

enabled.description: Whether the generated server limits API calls. The server-go generator writes the wiring only when it is set.

api_key.description: Calls per window per API key. Defaults to 5000 per 1m.

account.description: Calls per window per signed-in account. Defaults to 1000 per 1m.

tenant.description: Calls per window per tenant, across every account and key they have. What stops one customer crowding out the rest. Defaults to 10000 per 1m.

ip.description: Calls per window per source address, for callers who are not signed in. Only for those: once a request carries an identity that identity is the better key. Defaults to 300 per 1m.

interval.description: How long a replica may count locally before publishing to the database. The limiter can miss up to one interval of traffic per replica, and a shorter one costs writes. Defaults to 1s.

routes.description: Extra limits on particular route patterns, counted against the caller and on top of the per-caller limits.

exempt.description: Route patterns no limit applies to, for example a long-lived stream. Written as METHOD /path, matching the pattern the router registers.

pattern.description: The route pattern, as the router registers it — for example POST /api/v1/todos. Matched against the pattern net/http reports, not against the path.

max.description: How many calls are allowed in one window.

enabled.description: Whether the generated server, repositories and client open OpenTelemetry spans. Off means the generated code names no tracing library at all.

unmentioned_column.description: A column exists in the database but is not mentioned in its table configuration.

missing_comment.description: A table or column has no comment.

fk_needs_index.description: A foreign-key column is not covered by an index.

tenant_id_leading_index.description: No index leads with the tenant column.

boolean_prefix.description: A boolean column does not read as a predicate.

timestamp_suffix.description: A timestamp column is not named _at, or an _at column is not a timestamptz. A name ending in _at claims the column records when something happened, and only timestamptz can: a bare timestamp is a clock reading with nothing to anchor it.

date_suffix.description: A date column is not named _date, or a _date column is not a date.

fk_naming.description: A foreign-key column is not named after the table it references.

cascade_delete.description: A foreign key declares ON DELETE CASCADE.

migration_filename.description: A migration file is not named NNNNN_snake_case.sql.

project.description: Identity of the application being generated.

layout.description: Where table configuration and generated code live.

api.description: Shape of the generated HTTP API.

database.description: Where to run migrations and read the schema from.

auth.description: How the authentication foundation's tables are treated.

files.description: Where uploaded files are kept, and what an upload may be.

notifications.description: The inbox, and how notifications are delivered.

presence.description: Who is here, and what they are looking at.

throttle.description: How many API calls one caller may make. Fair-use limiting, counted in the database so replicas cannot disagree.

cache.description: Whether reads are held in memory between requests, behind a Postgres NOTIFY channel that invalidates them when the transaction causing it commits.

tracing.description: Whether the generated code emits OpenTelemetry spans.

monitoring.description: rig's own page over the spans this server wrote. It needs tracing.

naming.description: How database names become Go and JSON names.

validate.description: Severity of each configurable convention rule.

title: rig project configuration
description: Project-wide configuration: layout, database, naming, convention severities, and the generators to run.
